title: Amphipod
description: Move amphipods into their home rooms with minimum energy using Dijkstra.
writeup:
## Approach

Amphipods of four types (A, B, C, D) must reach their designated side rooms, moving through a shared hallway. Each type has a different movement cost (1, 10, 100, 1000). This is a shortest-path problem over game states.

The state is the set of all amphipod positions. Dijkstra's algorithm explores states in order of increasing energy cost. Move rules: amphipods in rooms can move to valid hallway positions (never stopping in front of a room); amphipods in the hallway can only move directly into their home room, and only if it contains no foreign types. They always move as deep as possible.

## Part 1

Rooms are 2 deep. The state space is manageable — positions are constrained to 7 hallway spots and 8 room slots. Dijkstra with a visited set finds the minimum energy.

## Part 2

Insert two extra rows (`#D#C#B#A#` and `#D#B#A#C#`) to make rooms 4 deep. The same algorithm handles the larger state space, though it takes longer due to more possible configurations.
